q: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and ____.
e: Cells divide on a regular basic to bring about growth and asexual reproduction. Asexual reproduction copies one parent, often through mitosis.

q: The cell cycle involves several different phases, including Interphase and the ____.
e: The cell cycle involves several different phases, including Interphase and the mitotic M phase. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division.

q: Interphase is subdivided into G$_1$, S and ____ stages.
e: Interphase is subdivided into G1, S and G2 stages. G2 is the growth and check stage after DNA has been copied. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied.

q: In G$_1$ stage, the ____ of cell takes place.
e: In G1 stage, the growth of cell takes place. Growth is the biological term this statement needs.

q: DNA replication is carried out in ____ stage.
e: DNA replication is carried out in S stage. DNA replication happens in S phase. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: After replication is completed each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called ____.
e: After replication is completed each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called chromatids. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the ____.
e: Chromatids are joined together at a point called the centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: In G$_2$ stage, the organelles are replicated and the ____ grows.
e: In G2 stage, the organelles are replicated and the cell grows. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function.

q: This is followed by mitosis, a period of active nuclear division and ____, the separation of cytoplasm.
e: This is followed by mitosis, a period of active nuclear division and cytokinesis, the separation of cytoplasm. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus.

q: Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors. When errors do occur, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of ____.
e: Cell division is a strictly regulated process that mostly works without errors. When errors do occur, they can be catastrophic and cause the development of cancer. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division after control checkpoints fail.

q: Interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the ____ phase.
e: Interphase, the initial stage of the cell cycle, used to be called the resting phase. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division.

q: Actually, it is not resting during interphase; the normal metabolic processes of the cell continue and new DNA is produced for the replication of ____.
e: Actually, it is not resting during interphase; the normal metabolic processes of the cell continue and new DNA is produced for the replication of chromosome. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA.

q: New proteins, cytoplasm and cell organelles are also made so that the cell is in the state of preparation to produce ____.
e: New proteins, cytoplasm and cell organelles are also made so that the cell is in the state of preparation to produce two new cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Many metabolic reactions run in the cytoplasm.

q: During the process of cell division, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided with the remaining contents of the cell to produce two identical ____.
e: During the process of cell division, the chromosomes that are duplicated during interphase are divided with the remaining contents of the cell to produce two identical daughter cells. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and ____.
e: Mitosis is divided into four phases: prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets. In metaphase chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate.

q: In prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete ____.
e: In prophase, the chromatins become more tightly coiled and condensing into discrete chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form.

q: Each early mitotic chromosome appears as two identical sister chromatids joined at their ____.
e: Each early mitotic chromosome appears as two identical sister chromatids joined at their centromeres. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed.

q: The spindles begin to form. The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called ____.
e: The spindles begin to form. The radial arrays of shorter microtubules around each centriole are called asters. Asters are microtubule arrays around the poles in animal mitosis.

q: The centrioles start moving to opposite ends of the cell, forming protein fibres between them called the ____.
e: The centrioles start moving to opposite ends of the cell, forming protein fibres between them called the spindles. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: The nuclear envelope breaks down and the ____ disappears.
e: The nuclear envelope breaks down and the nucleolus disappears. The nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase. The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase and reforms in telophase.

q: In metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the ____ of the cell.
e: In metaphase, the chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate of the cell. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its ____.
e: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids stay attached at the centromere.

q: In anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, ____ first, towards opposite poles of the cell.
e: In anaphase, the chromatids from each pair are pulled, centromere first, towards opposite poles of the cell. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: The centromeres divide, separating each pair of sister chromatids, due to contraction of ____.
e: The centromeres divide, separating each pair of sister chromatids, due to contraction of spindles. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: At the end of anaphase, the two sets of chromatids have been separated to opposite ends of the cell. The chromatids are now called ____.
e: At the end of anaphase, the two sets of chromatids have been separated to opposite ends of the cell. The chromatids are now called chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and ____ reform around the two sets of chromosomes.
e: During telophase, the spindle fibres break down and nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes. Two nuclear envelopes form in telophase. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: The ____ and centrioles are also re-formed.
e: The nucleoli and centrioles are also re-formed. Nucleoli is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The chromosomes begin to uncoil and becoming less dense, as in Figure 5.6.
e: The chromosomes begin to uncoil and becoming less dense, as in Figure 5.6. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: In animal cells, a ring of contractile fibres tightens around the centre of the cell similar to a belt tightening around a sack of ____.
e: In animal cells, a ring of contractile fibres tightens around the centre of the cell similar to a belt tightening around a sack of flour. Flour is the biological term this statement needs.

q: In plant cells, the division for the cell occurs differently. A ____ cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards.
e: In plant cells, the division for the cell occurs differently. A cellulose cell wall builds up from the inside of the cell outwards. Cellulose is the beta-glucose polymer that makes plant cell walls rigid. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function.

q: In both cases, the result is that two genetically identical ____ are formed.
e: In both cases, the result is that two genetically identical daughter cells are formed. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair.

q: Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in ____.
e: Meiosis is a type of nuclear division that happens only in sex organs. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Cells that divide by meiosis have the full number of chromosomes to start with, but the cells that are formed from meiosis have half the number. So it is called ____.
e: Cells that divide by meiosis have the full number of chromosomes to start with, but the cells that are formed from meiosis have half the number. So it is called reduction division. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: In animals, the gametes are formed directly from meiosis. The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called ____.
e: In animals, the gametes are formed directly from meiosis. The formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis, while that of ovum is called oogenesis. Oogenesis is meiosis that produces eggs. Spermatogenesis is meiosis that produces sperm.

q: In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called ____.
e: In flowering plants, meiosis forms special male cells called microspores and female cells called megaspores. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four ____ daughter cells.
e: In meiosis, two nuclear divisions produce four haploid daughter cells. Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes, as in gametes. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells.

q: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and ____.
e: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes.

q: In prophase I of meiosis, the two chromosomes of each pair, known as homologous pairs, stay close together in a process called ____.
e: In prophase I of meiosis, the two chromosomes of each pair, known as homologous pairs, stay close together in a process called synapsis. Synapsis is pairing of homologous chromosomes in meiosis I. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells.

q: At this stage, ____ introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine.
e: At this stage, crossing over introduces genetic variation as the chromatids may break and recombine. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation.

q: In anaphase I, the centromeres do not divide. One chromosome (pair of chromatids) from each homologous pair moves to each end of the cell. As a result, the chromosome number at each pole is ____ to that of the original numbers.
e: In anaphase I, the centromeres do not divide. One chromosome (pair of chromatids) from each homologous pair moves to each end of the cell. As a result, the chromosome number at each pole is half to that of the original numbers. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere.

q: In telophase I, the nuclear membrane re-forms and the cells begin to ____.
e: In telophase I, the nuclear membrane re-forms and the cells begin to divide. In telophase nuclei reform around the two chromosome sets.
